summary: CCC-built steel lookout erected in 1934 on Armintrout Road, Pike County, OH; moved in 2016 to the Ohio State Fairgrounds, where it is not open to unassisted visits.

facts.design: Steel CCC-built fire tower; legs re-galvanized, landings and stairs replaced with state-forest wood and cab refinished with new glass in 2016
facts.status_note: Dismantled and moved in 2016 to the ODNR Natural Resources Park on the Ohio State Fairgrounds, Columbus; now 60 feet to the bottom of the cab. No source describes the Pike County site today
facts.agency: Ohio Division of Forestry (NHLR administrator); displayed by the ODNR Natural Resources Park

access.note: Not open to unassisted public visits, per a 2016 Ohio's Country Journal article; current rules not confirmed

visit.trail_note: Stands right behind Smoky Bear in the ODNR Natural Resources Park on the Ohio State Fairgrounds, Columbus; check with ODNR before planning a visit

events.note: Erected by CCC crews on Armintrout Road in Pike County; the state paid $1 for .35 acres bought from the Armintrout family
Chillicothe Gazette item of October 27, 1934 says the new tower was being occupied by H. G. Armintrout of the Shyville community
Ownership passed to the Pike County Public Service Trust for civil defense purposes; the panels say Ohio's lookout network closed its last tower that year, and give no closing date for this tower
Dismantled and moved by Geiger Brothers LLC from Pike County to the ODNR Natural Resources Park on the Ohio State Fairgrounds
Shortened to 60 feet, measured from the ground to the bottom of the cab
Legs sandblasted, acid dipped and re-galvanized; wooden landings and stairs replaced with state-forest wood; cab refinished with new glass

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The panels give 80 feet for the original tower and Ohio's Country Journal gives 71 feet. Both say it is now 60 feet to the bottom of the cab. No original height is recorded.
Two 1934 Gazette items spell the landowner's name Armentrout; the 27 October 1934 Gazette item, the panels and the NHLR entry use Armintrout. Both spellings are kept in the record.

notes_for_editor: Covers both the original Pike County site and the 2016 move. Height conflicts (80 ft in the panels, 71 ft in the Country Journal article); the record carries no original height. Two of the Gazette items read on Forest Lookouts spell the landowner Armentrout; the 27 October 1934 item spells it Armintrout. Access rests on a 2016 article, so current rules need confirming with ODNR. The ODNR tower page returned 404 in an earlier cache and was not reread here. Nothing found describes what, if anything, remains at the Armintrout Road site. The sibling record us-oh-armintrout-at-ohio-exposition-center covers the tower at its current site.
